title: POC scoping - benchmark harness integration
summary: Redwood AE/SE and Acme HealthTech engineering discussed scoping a POC to validate latency and cost for a live inference workload. Focus: integrate Acme's benchmark harness and customer scripts into Redwood's test environment, define success criteria (p95 latency < 300ms for non-streaming, streaming latency SLA, cost per 1M tokens), workload sizing (concurrency, token distribution), and an execution timeline for a 3-week pilot with automation of load tests and monitoring.
action_items: Maya - share Redwood benchmark harness repo and README - 2025-09-12
Markus - provide representative request scripts and sample token distribution CSV - 2025-09-11
Sara - grant test VPC access and provide egress IP allowlist for Redwood runners - 2025-09-14
Liam - send draft POC statement of work and pricing estimate - 2025-09-13
next_steps: Redwood to onboard Acme's scripts into harness and run initial smoke test (non-streaming) - target 2025-09-16
Run 3 phased benchmarks: smoke, scale to expected concurrency, stress test with fallback scenarios - week of 2025-09-16
Schedule technical deep-dive to compare streaming vs non-streaming perf and cost impacts - 2025-09-18
Share SOC2/security docs and VPC onboarding checklist - 2025-09-12
transcript: Header: Date: 2025-09-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Rachel Lee (Acme CTO), Markus Vogel (Lead ML Eng), Sara Gomez (Infra)
00:00 - Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call?
00:06 - Rachel: Hi Rachel here, CTO at Acme HealthTech, excited to scope this POC.
00:10 - Markus: Markus, ML eng, I'll own the scripts and metrics on our side.
00:14 - Sara: Sara, infra, I'll handle VPC and networking for tests.
00:18 - Maya: Maya from Redwood, I'll lead the harness integration and perf tests, quick note: some transcriptions may show Redwood product names weirdly in logs.
02:05 - Liam: Goal for today is to align on success criteria, workload sizing and the harness integration approach, especially streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs.

03:12 - Rachel: Our primary success criteria: p95 latency below 300ms for the non-streaming API at expected load, and predictable cost metrics; also data residency and SOC2 compliance are gating factors.

04:00 - Markus: Our workload: baseline is 500 RPS bursty with average request size 600 tokens, tail to 800 tokens for some flows. Concurrent users roughly 150 active sessions, but traffic patterns are spiky during morning syncs.
04:42 - Maya: Good, so two axes: token distribution and concurrency. We'll want your exact token histogram; Markus can send a sample CSV of request sizes.
05:10 - Markus: I'll export that today, expect a CSV with percentiles, plus a few real request payloads for the harness.
06:25 - Liam: For benchmarks we typically track p50/p95/p99, throughput (req/s), tokens/s, and cost per 1M tokens. Also stabilization under steady-state for 10-15 minutes per step.

07:00 - Rachel: For us p99 isn't as critical as p95, but we need predictable SLOs. Also want to test degradation modes - if Dedicated capacity is saturated, does Redwood fall back to hosted or lower-quality quantized variants?
07:48 - Maya: We can test fallbacks: route policy to model variant, and observe latency/cost impacts. For POC we'll instrument both throughput and the routing decisions in traces.
09:30 - Sara: Networking: we need list of Redwood runner egress IPs for allowlist. We prefer VPC peering but can do IP allowlist for short-term POC.

10:12 - Liam: We'll send the allowlist and the VPC onboarding checklist. For the harness integration we support Locust and our internal runner; we can also run your JMeter scripts but Locust tends to handle streaming better.
11:00 - Markus: Our current harness is a mix of Python scripts and JMeter; we can convert a couple of critical flows to Locust if you provide examples.

11:30 - Maya: We'll share a sample Locust task and the benchmark harness README. Integration steps: ingest your request scripts, map auth/token injection, and create a token-size distribution generator.
12:10 - Liam: Important to decide streaming vs non-streaming early: streaming can reduce perceived latency for long responses, but streaming paths change resource usage and throughput calculations.

13:02 - Markus: For some UX flows users need first-token times under 150ms; that's where streaming helps. But for billing and cost comparison we need both end-to-end non-streaming and streaming traces.

13:45 - Maya: Agreed - plan: run paired tests for key flows. Non-streaming: measure p95 end-to-end. Streaming: measure first-token latency and tail for token emission rate. We'll also compare token-cost delta between the two.
15:20 - Rachel: Any constraints on model versions? We need to pin a model for the POC, probably an open model you have verified. Also interested in quantized variants for cost saving.
16:00 - Maya: We'll propose two variants: a float16 baseline and an int8 quantized variant where supported. We'll document quality delta with a small eval set you provide.
17:12 - Sara: Regarding security: we need SOC2 docs, encryption at rest with KMS, and SAML/SSO integration details for access to the Redwood console.
17:45 - Liam: We'll send SOC2 and SSO docs, plus steps for KMS integration in Private/Dedicated modes. For POC we'll likely use a short-lived test key and audit logs enabled.
19:00 - Markus: For harness orchestration, can Redwood run tests from your hosted runners in our VPC? Or do we run Locust in our infra against Redwood endpoints?

19:35 - Maya: Both are possible. Best path for short POC: you run Locust inside your test VPC hitting Redwood hosted endpoints in a dedicated test pool we allocate; alternatively we can spin up a runner that peeks into your VPC via peering.

20:50 - Liam: Timeline check: client wants a 3-week pilot. Week 1: onboarding and smoke tests. Week 2: scale tests and streaming/non-stream comparison. Week 3: stress tests, cost analysis, and wrap up findings.
22:15 - Rachel: That matches our expectations. Are there measurable pass/fail criteria? We want to avoid ambiguous outcomes.

22:35 - Maya: Proposed pass criteria: 1) Non-streaming p95 < 300ms at target concurrency and token distribution; 2) Streaming first-token < 150ms for streaming flows; 3) Cost per 1M tokens within 20% of estimate; 4) No data egress or retention policy violations and VPC + SOC2 checks passed.
24:00 - Markus: On tooling, we need the CSV output format for time-series of metrics so we can ingest into our dashboards; do you provide raw traces and JSON logs?
24:30 - Maya: Yes, we provide per-request traces, aggregated histograms, and raw event logs. We'll share the expected CSV/JSON schemas so Markus can wire them into your dashboards.
26:10 - Sara: For network egress allowlist, we prefer a CIDR range. Is that possible or just IPs per runner?
26:35 - Liam: We'll provide a short-lived CIDR for the runners for the POC window; exact details in the VPC checklist.
28:00 - Rachel: About costs: do you have tooling to estimate token cost for projected volume? We need a ballpark to present to finance.
28:20 - Liam: We'll include a cost model in the SOW: tokens per request * requests/day => monthly token estimate and estimated USD cost for each model variant and quantization option.
29:15 - Markus: Any limitations on sequence length? Some of our docs queries are 2k-3k tokens.
29:45 - Maya: We support up to 8k in the POC tier for most models; kernel selection will vary. We'll note expected performance degradation for long sequences and include that in the plan.
31:00 - Rachel: Who will own the test runs and the analysis?
31:20 - Liam: Redwood will run initial smoke tests and the scale phase in collaboration; final analysis will be co-authored and we'll present a findings deck at the end.
33:00 - Maya: Small gotcha: transcription note, sometimes product names appear as 'Red wood' in logs; ignore those typos when mapping metrics back to models.
34:10 - Markus: For the harness, I'd like an example Locust task that includes streaming client behavior (event callbacks for token chunks).
34:45 - Maya: We'll include two examples: non-streaming request task and streaming client that records first-token timestamps and per-chunk throughput.
36:00 - Rachel: Agree to the proposed action items and timeline, want a short SOW and kickoff email after this call.
36:30 - Liam: I'll draft the SOW and send by Friday - it'll include steps, success criteria, pricing for the POC pool and optional Dedicated test capacity.
38:00 - Sara: Note on compliance: we'll need audit log retention settings during the POC window to be at least 90 days for our auditors.
38:28 - Liam: We can enable 90-day retention for the POC audit logs - we'll include that in the checklist.
40:00 - Rachel: Any blockers we foresee?
40:18 - Markus: Main blocker is getting the token distribution and scripts; otherwise it's mostly coordination on VPC allowlist.
40:45 - Maya: If we get the scripts by 2025-09-11 and VPC info by 2025-09-14 we can stick to the timeline.
42:00 - Liam: Quick recap of next steps and owners...
42:10 - Maya: I'll share the harness repo link, README, and sample Locust tasks (Maya - 2025-09-12).
42:30 - Markus: I'll deliver the token distribution CSV and example payloads (Markus - 2025-09-11).
42:50 - Sara: Provide VPC allowlist / peering details (Sara - 2025-09-14).
43:20 - Liam: I'll send the SOW and cost estimate (Liam - 2025-09-13) and SOC2 docs today after the call.
44:00 - Rachel: Sounds good, schedule tech deep dive for streaming details on 2025-09-18.
44:20 - Liam: Will send calendar invite for the 9/18 deep-dive, and initial smoke test window for 9/16.
45:00 - Meeting end: thanks everyone!
